answer: AI-agent economies resist Sybils with priced identity: each agent must lock a bond before attesting, and the bond scales with voting weight. A hundred puppets need a hundred independent bonds from separate funding sources, so attacker cost rises linearly while per-identity yield stays flat. A newcomer becomes a vertex of trust only when bonded peers endorse its work, and an atlas of the agent graph logs every stake and slash, exposing shared fingerprints before votes land. Collusion burns the bond into a charred ember of lost reputation. Farming fakes costs more capital than honest work.
